families.title: Transit access
families.mechanism: Reduces what riders pay, or extends an existing assistance formula to places a provider does not serve.

structuralProvenance.reference: House Transportation and Infrastructure hearing record CHRG-117hhrg45093
structuralProvenance.establishes: Infrastructure argument in a real hearing record recurs around maintenance backlog, rural access, broadband, water and named local projects, and members ask for locally important provisions inside a larger package.

structuralProvenance.reference: Senate Amendment 2638 to Senate Amendment 2137, 117th Congress
structuralProvenance.establishes: A narrow targeted section can be drafted, sponsored and laid on the table without ever entering the enacted text, so proposed text and adopted text are different records.

intendedOutcome.statement: Whether removing the fare actually moves boardings by riders who qualify.

evidence.note: Any figure for additional boardings under this Act would be a projection, not a count.
evidence.unavailableReason: Nobody has counted boardings here, so a projection would have nothing to move.

variants.label: Fare relief for assistance enrollees
variants.synopsis: Riders already enrolled in a state assistance program ride without paying a fare, and participating providers are reimbursed in proportion to those boardings.
declaredLimits: It creates no entitlement to service, and does not require any provider to add a route.
It reimburses boardings; it does not fund vehicles, staff or maintenance.

evidence.note: An authored ceiling for a fictional state pilot. It is not drawn from any real transit budget and is not a measured cost.

options.label: Riders enrolled in state assistance
options.clausePhrase: enrolled in a state assistance program at the time of boarding

options.label: Assistance enrollees and secondary students
options.clausePhrase: enrolled in a state assistance program at the time of boarding, or enrolled in a public secondary school

options.label: Assistance enrollees and riders over sixty-five
options.clausePhrase: enrolled in a state assistance program at the time of boarding, or sixty-five years of age or older

evidence.note: Authored eligibility classes for a fictional program. No real state's assistance rules are asserted.
An authored pilot length. It is a design choice, not a finding about how long such a pilot needs to run.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to test whether removing the fare barrier increases access to work, care and school for riders who already qualify for state assistance. Nothing in this Act creates an entitlement to service.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A rider is eligible under this Act if the rider is {{choice:rider-eligibility}}. A participating provider shall not require a separate application.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every rider {{choice:rider-eligibility}}

rendering.text: There is appropriated for the {{years-attributive:pilot-term}} pilot a sum not to exceed {{money:support-limit}}, to be distributed among participating providers in proportion to eligible boardings. No provider is named in this section.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every participating provider, in proportion to eligible boardings

rendering.text: There is appropriated for the pilot a sum not to exceed {{money:support-limit}}, to be distributed among participating providers in proportion to eligible boardings. No provider is named in this section.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every participating provider, in proportion to eligible boardings

amendmentInvitation.heading: Local project match
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: The authority cannot raise the local match that pilot participation requires, and without it the county's riders get nothing from a statewide program.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member on behalf of a fictional authority. No real transit authority has asked for anything.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts appropriated by Section 3 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be awarded to the Ashland–Boyd County Transit Authority as the local match required for pilot participation, and an award under this section shall not reduce the amount available to any other participating provider.

variants.label: Formula access for unserved counties
variants.synopsis: Counties with no fixed-route provider become eligible for the existing transit assistance formula, which today reaches only counties that already have service.
declaredLimits: It changes who the formula reaches. It does not change the formula's rate, and it does not create service where no provider applies.
It sets no fare policy for any rider.

evidence.note: An authored addition to a fictional formula. No real state formula amount is asserted.

options.label: Counties with no fixed-route provider
options.clausePhrase: in which no fixed-route provider operated during the preceding fiscal year

options.label: Counties with neither fixed-route nor demand-response service
options.clausePhrase: in which neither a fixed-route provider nor a demand-response provider operated during the preceding fiscal year

evidence.note: Authored service tests for a fictional formula. No county is identified and no service inventory is claimed.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to extend the transit assistance formula to counties the formula does not currently reach. Nothing in this Act obliges a county to establish service or a provider to apply.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A county is eligible for distribution under the transit assistance formula if it is a county {{choice:county-test}}. Eligibility under this section does not displace a county already receiving a distribution.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every county {{choice:county-test}}

rendering.text: There is appropriated to the transit assistance formula a sum not to exceed {{money:formula-addition}} for distribution to counties made eligible by this Act, distributed on the same basis as to any other eligible county.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every county made eligible by this Act, on the formula's existing basis

amendmentInvitation.heading: Hold-harmless for currently served counties
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: counties already drawing a formula distribution
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: Counties that built service on the formula should not lose ground because the formula was widened, and members from those counties will not vote to widen it otherwise.

evidence.note: An authored counter-ask from fictional members. No county has made this request.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts appropriated by Section 3 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be used to hold harmless a county whose distribution would otherwise fall below its distribution for the preceding fiscal year.

families.title: Bridge and culvert maintenance
families.mechanism: Makes an inspection condition rating the operative test for which structures a maintenance program may reach.

structuralProvenance.reference: House Transportation and Infrastructure hearing record CHRG-117hhrg45093
structuralProvenance.establishes: Infrastructure argument in a real hearing record recurs around maintenance backlog, rural access, broadband, water and named local projects, and members ask for locally important provisions inside a larger package.
An official estimate distinguishes authorizing legislation from appropriation treatment and states which effects it did not model, rather than presenting one confident total.

intendedOutcome.statement: Whether repair or preventive treatment holds average structure condition.

evidence.note: Any figure for structures kept out of the worst rating band would be a projection.
evidence.unavailableReason: No department has been asked to report structure condition here, so there is nothing to project from.

variants.label: Worst-first repair
variants.synopsis: Only structures an inspection has already rated at or below a stated condition are eligible, and the program reports each year on what it reached and what it did not.
declaredLimits: It reaches structures by rating alone. A structure nobody has inspected is not eligible, because there is no rating to test.
It funds repair, not replacement, and requires no new inspection program.

evidence.note: An authored authorization ceiling for a fictional state program. No real maintenance backlog cost is asserted.

parameters.label: Eligible at or below condition rating

evidence.note: An authored rating scale for this game. It is not the National Bridge Inventory scale and no real structure's rating is claimed.

parameters.label: What the annual report must contain

options.label: Structures reached and structures still eligible
options.clausePhrase: the structures repaired under this Act and the structures that remained eligible at the close of the year

options.label: Reached, remaining, and what was deferred and why
options.clausePhrase: the structures repaired under this Act, the structures that remained eligible at the close of the year, and each structure whose repair was deferred together with the reason for the deferral

evidence.note: An authored reporting duty. No real reporting statute is reproduced.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to direct repair funds to the structures an inspection has already found to be in the worst condition. Nothing in this Act requires an inspection to be carried out.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A bridge or culvert on the state-maintained system is eligible for repair under this Act if its most recent recorded inspection assigned it a condition rating of {{integer:condition-threshold}} or below. A structure with no recorded inspection is not eligible under this section.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every state-maintained structure rated {{integer:condition-threshold}} or below at its most recent inspection

rendering.text: There is authorized for repair of eligible structures a sum not to exceed {{money:repair-authorization}}. An amount authorized by this section is available only for repair, and confers no obligation until it is appropriated.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every eligible structure, without preference

rendering.text: The department shall report annually to the legislature {{choice:annual-report}}. The report shall be public.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: the legislature and the public

amendmentInvitation.heading: Set-aside for locally maintained structures
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: county-maintained bridges in the eastern counties
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: The worst structures in these counties are county-maintained and therefore fall outside a state-system program entirely, which is the reason their ratings are the lowest.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. No county's structures or ratings are real.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts authorized by Section 3 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be made available for repair of county-maintained structures in counties whose average recorded condition rating is below the statewide average.

variants.label: Preventive treatment cycle
variants.synopsis: Structures still in fair or better condition are treated on a fixed cycle to keep them from failing, and a structure that has already failed is handled elsewhere.
declaredLimits: It deliberately does not reach the worst structures. A structure at or below the threshold leaves this program rather than entering it.
It sets a treatment cycle; it does not guarantee any structure is treated in a given year.

evidence.note: An authored authorization ceiling for a fictional program. It is not a measured preventive-maintenance cost.
An authored rating scale for this game, on the same fictional scale as the repair variant.
An authored cycle length. It is a design choice, not an engineering finding.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to treat structures before they fail, on the premise that deferred treatment becomes replacement. Nothing in this Act reaches a structure that has already fallen below the condition this Act requires.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A bridge or culvert on the state-maintained system is eligible for preventive treatment under this Act if its most recent recorded inspection assigned it a condition rating above {{integer:condition-floor}}. A structure whose rating falls to {{integer:condition-floor}} or below ceases to be eligible under this Act.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every state-maintained structure rated above {{integer:condition-floor}} at its most recent inspection

rendering.text: The department shall establish a preventive treatment cycle under which each eligible structure is considered for treatment at least once every {{years-phrase:cycle-years}}. Consideration under this section does not oblige treatment in a given year.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every eligible structure, on the adopted cycle

rendering.text: The department shall establish a preventive treatment cycle for eligible structures and shall publish the cycle it adopts.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every eligible structure, on the adopted cycle

rendering.text: There is authorized for preventive treatment of eligible structures a sum not to exceed {{money:treatment-authorization}}. An amount authorized by this section confers no obligation until it is appropriated.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every eligible structure, without preference

amendmentInvitation.heading: Deferred treatment on low-volume routes
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: low-volume routes in the western counties
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: A uniform cycle spends the same on a structure carrying forty vehicles a day as on one carrying four thousand, and the counties with the low-volume routes are the ones with the least other road money.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. No traffic counts or routes are real.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts authorized by Section 4 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be made available to extend the treatment cycle on routes carrying fewer vehicles than the statewide median, without reducing the amount available on any other route.

families.title: Broadband access
families.mechanism: Attaches a minimum service standard and a reporting duty to public support for internet service.

structuralProvenance.reference: House Transportation and Infrastructure hearing record CHRG-117hhrg45093
structuralProvenance.establishes: Infrastructure argument in a real hearing record recurs around maintenance backlog, rural access, broadband, water and named local projects, and members ask for locally important provisions inside a larger package.
An official estimate distinguishes authorizing legislation from appropriation treatment and states which effects it did not model, rather than presenting one confident total.

intendedOutcome.statement: Whether the share of households that can and do take service actually rises.

evidence.note: Any figure for households newly served or newly subscribing would be a projection.
evidence.unavailableReason: Nobody has measured who can get service here, or who takes it, so a projection would have nothing to start from.

variants.label: Buildout to unserved areas
variants.synopsis: Public support goes to construction in areas below a stated service level, and anything built with it must meet a minimum standard and report against it.
declaredLimits: It supports construction. It does not reduce what any household pays.
It sets a standard the recipient must meet; it does not regulate any provider that takes no money under this Act.

evidence.note: An authored authorization ceiling for a fictional program. No real buildout cost is asserted.
An authored service threshold for this game. It is not any regulator's definition of unserved.

options.label: A download and upload speed
options.clausePhrase: deliver the download and upload speeds stated in its award agreement

options.label: Speed and a latency ceiling
options.clausePhrase: deliver the download and upload speeds stated in its award agreement and keep round-trip latency below the ceiling stated in that agreement

options.label: Speed, latency, and a published price
options.clausePhrase: deliver the download and upload speeds stated in its award agreement, keep round-trip latency below the ceiling stated in that agreement, and publish and honor the price stated in that agreement

evidence.note: Authored obligations for a fictional award agreement. No real award terms are reproduced.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to support construction of internet service in areas that do not have it, on terms that survive the construction. Nothing in this Act obliges a provider to seek an award.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: An area is eligible for an award under this Act if no provider offers service in that area at a download speed of {{integer:unserved-threshold}} megabits per second or greater. An area's eligibility is determined as of the date the award is made.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every area without service at {{integer:unserved-threshold}} megabits per second or greater

rendering.text: A recipient of an award under this Act shall {{choice:service-standard}}, and shall report annually on its performance against that obligation. Failure to report is itself a breach of the award agreement.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every household in an area built with an award under this Act

rendering.text: There is authorized for awards under this Act a sum not to exceed {{money:buildout-authorization}}. An award may not exceed the cost of construction stated in the application it is made on.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every eligible area, by application

amendmentInvitation.heading: Preference for cooperative applicants
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: The cooperatives are the only applicants that have ever built in these counties, and a scoring system written for large carriers will not reach them.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. No cooperative has applied for anything.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts authorized by Section 4 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be reserved for awards to applicants organized as cooperatives, and a reservation under this section shall not reduce the amount available to any other eligible applicant.

variants.label: Household adoption support
variants.synopsis: Eligible households get help paying for service that already reaches them, and providers report take-up rather than construction.
declaredLimits: It builds nothing. A household in an area with no service at all gets nothing from this Act.
It supports subscriptions; it sets no speed a provider must deliver.

evidence.note: An authored authorization ceiling for a fictional program. No real subsidy total is asserted.

options.label: Households enrolled in state assistance
options.clausePhrase: in which a member is enrolled in a state assistance program

options.label: Assistance households and school-meal households
options.clausePhrase: in which a member is enrolled in a state assistance program, or in which a child qualifies for a free or reduced-price school meal

evidence.note: Authored eligibility classes for a fictional program. No real assistance rules are asserted.

options.label: How many eligible households enrolled
options.clausePhrase: the number of eligible households enrolled in each county

options.label: Enrollments and disconnections
options.clausePhrase: the number of eligible households enrolled in each county and the number disconnected for non-payment during the year

evidence.note: An authored reporting duty. No real provider reporting is reproduced.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to help households pay for internet service that already reaches them, on the premise that service nobody subscribes to is not access. Nothing in this Act supports construction.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A household is eligible for support under this Act if it is a household {{choice:household-test}} and service is available at its address. A provider shall not require a separate application from a household the department certifies.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every household {{choice:household-test}} at an address service reaches

rendering.text: A provider receiving support under this Act shall report annually {{choice:take-up-report}}. The report shall be public in aggregate and shall not identify a household.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: the legislature and the public, in aggregate

rendering.text: There is appropriated for support under this Act a sum not to exceed {{money:adoption-authorization}}, applied to the subscription of an eligible household and paid to the provider serving it.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every eligible household that enrolls

amendmentInvitation.heading: Outreach in structurally unserved communities
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: households in communities the certification never reaches
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the communities without a county certification office
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: Certification is done at county offices, and the households furthest from one are exactly the households this Act is supposed to reach.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. No community or office is real.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts appropriated by Section 4 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be used for certification outreach in communities without a county certification office, and outreach under this section shall not reduce support available to any eligible household.

families.title: Water service lines
families.mechanism: Imposes a dated compliance duty on water systems, with or without money attached to discharging it.

structuralProvenance.reference: House Transportation and Infrastructure hearing record CHRG-117hhrg45093
structuralProvenance.establishes: Infrastructure argument in a real hearing record recurs around maintenance backlog, rural access, broadband, water and named local projects, and members ask for locally important provisions inside a larger package.

structuralProvenance.reference: Senate Amendment 2638 to Senate Amendment 2137, 117th Congress
structuralProvenance.establishes: A narrow targeted section can be drafted, sponsored and laid on the table without ever entering the enacted text, so proposed text and adopted text are different records.

intendedOutcome.statement: How many service lines are identified, and how many are replaced.

evidence.note: The inventory this Act requires is the thing that would produce the number; the number does not exist before it.
evidence.unavailableReason: No system has filed an inventory yet, which is what this Act is for.

variants.label: Inventory and replacement plan
variants.synopsis: Water systems above a stated size must inventory their service lines and file a replacement plan by a deadline. The Act appropriates nothing.
declaredLimits: It appropriates nothing and reimburses nothing. The cost of complying falls on the system.
It requires a plan to be filed. It does not require a single line to be replaced.

evidence.note: An authored size threshold for a fictional program. No real system's size is asserted.
An authored compliance window. It is a design choice, not a finding about how long an inventory takes.

options.label: A material inventory
options.clausePhrase: an inventory identifying the material of each service line in the system

options.label: Inventory and a replacement sequence
options.clausePhrase: an inventory identifying the material of each service line in the system and the sequence in which the system would replace them

options.label: Inventory, sequence, and the system's own cost estimate
options.clausePhrase: an inventory identifying the material of each service line in the system, the sequence in which the system would replace them, and the system's own estimate of the cost of doing so

evidence.note: An authored filing duty. No real inventory rule is reproduced.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to establish what the state's water systems are made of before deciding what replacing them would cost. Nothing in this Act appropriates money or obliges a system to replace a service line.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A community water system serving {{integer-locale:system-size}} or more connections is subject to this Act. A system below that size may file under this Act voluntarily and is not subject to its deadline.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every community water system serving {{integer-locale:system-size}} or more connections

clauses.heading: Filing deadline

rendering.text: A covered system shall file the plan required by this Act not later than {{date:endsOn}}. A system that has not filed by that date shall report the reason to the department.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every covered system, on the same date

clauses.textWhenNoEndDate: A covered system shall file the plan required by this Act, and the department shall publish the date by which it must be filed.

rendering.text: The plan required by this Act shall contain {{choice:plan-contents}}. The department shall publish each filed plan.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every household served by a covered system, through the published plan

amendmentInvitation.heading: Assistance for the smallest covered systems
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: the smallest systems this Act newly covers
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the small towns just over the threshold
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: A town just over the threshold has the same filing duty as a city and no engineer on staff to discharge it, and the duty is unfunded.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. It is the ask that would turn an unfunded mandate into a funded one, and nothing in the world says it was granted.

amendmentInvitation.text: Notwithstanding the absence of an appropriation elsewhere in this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be appropriated to assist covered systems in the smallest quartile by connections with the cost of preparing the plan this Act requires.

variants.label: Funded replacement program
variants.synopsis: Covered systems may draw on a replacement fund, with priority written into the statute rather than left to the department.
declaredLimits: It funds replacement for covered systems. A system below the size threshold draws nothing.
It sets a priority order; it does not guarantee any system is reached.

evidence.note: An authored fund ceiling for a fictional program. No real replacement cost is asserted.
An authored size threshold, on the same fictional basis as the inventory variant.

options.label: Systems with the highest share of covered lines
options.clausePhrase: to the systems with the highest share of service lines identified as requiring replacement

options.label: Systems with the least ability to pay
options.clausePhrase: to the systems whose residential rates would rise the most if the replacement were funded from rates alone

evidence.note: An authored priority rule. No real allocation rule is reproduced.

rendering.text: It is the purpose of this Act to fund replacement of the service lines a filed plan has identified, in an order the statute itself states. Nothing in this Act obliges a system to replace a line the fund does not reach.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone the Act reaches

rendering.text: A community water system serving {{integer-locale:system-size}} or more connections that has filed a replacement plan may draw on the fund established by this Act.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every community water system serving {{integer-locale:system-size}} or more connections that has filed a plan

rendering.text: There is appropriated to a service line replacement fund a sum not to exceed {{money:replacement-fund}}, available to covered systems that have filed a replacement plan.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every covered system that has filed a plan

rendering.text: The department shall distribute from the fund {{choice:priority-order}}, and shall publish the order it applies each year. A system's place in the order is not a guarantee of a distribution.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every covered system, in the stated order

amendmentInvitation.heading: Priority for schools and childcare premises
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: A priority order written around whole systems can leave a school at the back of its own system's queue, and members will not defend that to a parent.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. No school or premises is real.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amounts appropriated by Section 3 of this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} may be reserved for replacement of service lines serving school and licensed childcare premises, ahead of the order stated in Section 4.
